name: Ghana
prevalence_note: Bank of Ghana fraud reports and a 2026 consumer notice flag SIM-swap takeovers of bank and MoMo accounts, and tell the public that no bank or e-money issuer will ask for a PIN, password or OTP by phone, SMS or social media. The Cyber Security Authority also warns about prize-style MoMo calls.
cross_border_note: Calls are usually in English or a Ghanaian language and may spoof local mobile numbers or look like an operator care line.

scams.name: SIM-swap takeover of a bank or MoMo account
scams.name_en: SIM-swap takeover of a bank or MoMo account

red_flag_keywords.text: presses for a same-day SIM replacement on a cold call
solicits the one-time password tied to a new SIM
asks for an image of the national identity card

scams.signals_en: Criminals social-engineer a SIM replacement for a number that is tied to a bank app or mobile-money wallet, then use the taken-over line to approve withdrawals or reset access.
scams.legit_en: Bank of Ghana's industry fraud report describes SIM-swap as a route into bank and e-money accounts and notes that issuers must freeze an e-money account after a SIM change until valid ID is presented. NCA rules also treat unauthorised SIM activity as fraud.
bait_tactics: I have not been to an official shop to request a new SIM, and I am not approving a swap over a cold call.
The NCA registration guide on this phone will not open, and I am not sending Ghana Card images in this chat.
My MTN line is still receiving ordinary SMS, so I have no reason to treat this as an emergency replacement.

scams.name: MoMo PIN, OTP or Ghana Card vishing
scams.name_en: MoMo PIN, OTP or Ghana Card vishing

red_flag_keywords.text: solicits the MoMo PIN from a claimed help-desk caller
asks the customer to read a one-time password from an SMS
asks for Ghana Card particulars on the call

scams.signals_en: Unsolicited calls, texts or social-media messages claim to come from a bank, MoMo issuer or network and press the customer to reveal a PIN, password, OTP or Ghana Card particulars.
scams.legit_en: A Bank of Ghana notice dated 7 October 2026 states that no legitimate bank, mobile-money operator or payment service provider will request a PIN, password or OTP by phone, text, email or social media, and Ghana Card details should not be given to strangers.
bait_tactics: The MoMo app on this handset is still on the splash screen, and I am not reciting a PIN to someone who rang me.
No verification SMS has arrived on this Vodafone line, so I have no OTP to read.
My Ghana Card is in a drawer in the other room, and I am not describing it to an unknown caller.

scams.name: Fake MoMo prize or cash-award call
scams.name_en: Fake MoMo prize or cash-award call

red_flag_keywords.text: asks for a MoMo transfer as a condition of collecting a prize
asks for the wallet number so a supposed award can be paid
requires a processing charge before any prize is released

scams.signals_en: A caller or odd-looking SMS says the person has won a cash prize or MoMo bonus and then asks for a wallet transfer, account details, or a fee before the 'winnings' can be released.
scams.legit_en: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority warns the public to beware of scam calls that ask someone to send mobile money in order to receive a cash prize, or that request account details, and to use the official customer-service number when in doubt.
bait_tactics: I have not joined any MoMo raffle on this number, so I am not sending money to collect a prize.
The alleged winning notice came from an ordinary phone number, not from a short code I already know.
There is no spare e-cedi in this wallet for a processing charge, and I do not pay in advance for a gift.
